title: Cairnflow Service Protocol conformance trace
description: One file = one scenario: the frame conversation between runtime and SDK, the expected final journal, the wire version and the transport mode. Semantics: conformance/README.md.

source.description: The (Rust) test harness the scenario was taken from.

spec.description: The sections of docs/protocol-v1.md the scenario checks.

matrix_cells.description: Cells of the 'Mandatory tests' matrix in protocol-v1.md §10 (1 bit-exact replay, 2 out-of-order notifications, 3 run/ack ordering, 4 journal mismatch).

wire_version.description: The negotiated wire version. The runner sends content-type application/vnd.cairnflow.invocation.v<N>.

segments.description: Wire v6 traces only: the segments the runner serves — GET url ⇒ 200 with exactly the hex bytes. The SDK fetches them from Start.segment_urls and checks sha256 and length.

sdk_max_protocol_version.description: version-too-new traces only: the runner pins the SDK's maxProtocolVersion at this number (below wire_version) yet still sends content-type v<wire_version> — the deployment settled on the newer version, the SDK process was downgraded to an older release. No negotiation.

clock_ms.description: The SDK's wall clock, fixed for the whole trace (ms since the epoch). ctx.sleep(ms) journals clock_ms + ms.

initial_journal_len.description: Number of entries durable before the first connection (1 = only Input). Greater than 1: a new leader picked up the journal.

connections.description: In order. BIDI_STREAM: one h2c stream. REQUEST_RESPONSE: one HTTP request — every runtime frame is the request body, every SDK frame is the response body.

journal.description: The expected final journal, from entry 0 (Input).

status.description: The SDK must refuse the connection with this HTTP status (a too-new wire version: 415), no frames.

verify.description: true = a verifying connection: the runtime replays the whole final journal and the SDK may only return End (§10 'End is not a journal entry').

close.description: Who ends it. sdk: the SDK closes its side after the last frame. runtime: the runtime closes the stream (what the SDK waits for can only be answered by the outside world) and the SDK must close too without sending any further journal frame.

replay.description: Wire v5 (protocol-v1.md §9.3, v5 traces only): sdk_restart = the runner restarts the SDK (dropping its replay cache) before this connection; miss = the SDK must return 409 + header cairn-replay: miss, an empty body, no frames; cache = the value of the cairn-replay-cache header the SDK must return (absent = the SDK must not return that header).

stale_sdk.description: Round 2: this connection (and every later one) goes to a stale SDK replica — one that received every earlier connection except the last 200 one.

held.description: Round 2: the k of the cairn-replay-held header the SDK must return with 409.

held_digest.description: Round 2: the h_k (hex) of the cairn-replay-held header.

channel.description: journal: the frame belongs to the ordered stream of the invocation. side: side channel — never becomes a journal entry, never waits for a durable ack, changes nothing in the journal wherever it is interleaved (protocol-v1.md §9.2).

hex.description: The whole frame on the wire: 8-byte header + payload.

match.description: How an SDK frame is compared. Absent = bytes (whole frame, byte by byte). type: only the first 4 header bytes (type + flags) — the payload carries text the SDK chooses itself. error: like type, plus ErrorMessage.code and .behavior.

summary.description: A decoding for human readers; not part of the contract.
